findings.subject: TractTube.tsx:364-373 + 459-473 — the 'shared frame driver' token is a PER-INSTANCE ref, so every mounted tube dispatches the whole registry
findings.field: useTractFrameDriver() / frameDriverRef (module registry tractFrameRegistry)
findings.claimed: TractTube.tsx:30-39 states: 'Every mounted tube now publishes its animation state into the module-level tractFrameRegistry, and exactly ONE of them claims the frame driver (the first to commit) which advances the whole registry in insertion order … The remaining tubes' callbacks are a single null check.' The per-frame cost is documented as one callback (QUALITY_PLAN §3 item 10: 'the emissive/opacity lerp used to run in ONE useFrame callback PER TUBE (19 registrations)').
findings.expected: Exactly one mounted tube's useFrame callback runs stepAllTracts per frame; every other tube's callback returns immediately on a null token; the emissive/opacity lerp therefore applies the documented alpha (min(1, delta*8) ≈ 0.133 at 60 fps) ONCE per frame, giving the documented fade.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction between the documented contract and the shipped code. `useTractFrameDriver()` (TractTube.tsx:364-372) returns `useRef<TractFrameStep|null>(null)` — a ref created per component INSTANCE, not a module-level token — and TractTube.tsx:468 is `if (frameDriverRef.current === null) frameDriverRef.current = stepAllTracts`. Each instance's own ref is null at its first commit, so EVERY mounted tube claims its own token and its own useFrame callback calls stepAllTracts. Measured instance count (shipped tables, all layers on): 46 tract (23 records, 23 paired) + 24 nerve (12 + 12 mirrored) + 79 vessel (41 + 38 mirrored) = 149 tubes; at the documented default framing (brainstem-focus: vasculature region off) 70 tubes. So the pass runs N times per frame and iterates N entries: 149 × 149 = 22,201 stepTractFrame calls per frame at all-on (≈1.33 M/s at 60 fps) instead of 149. Measured lerp consequence: alpha = min(1, (1/60)*8) = 0.1333 is applied 149 times per frame, so the remaining fraction of a fade is (1-0.1333)^149 = 5.5e-10 — the documented 'softer' select/dim fade is a one-frame snap. tractFrameRegistrySize() is exported for diagnostics but is referenced by no gate (grep over scripts/ finds no tractFrameRegistry consumer), so nothing measures this.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the token module-level (e.g. `let driverOwner: symbol|null = null` plus an instance id, or claim the driver in the registry entry itself so the FIRST map entry owns the pass) and hand it over in the unmount cleanup; alternatively drop the token entirely and register ONE driver from a component that mounts with the tube family (e.g. SceneLayers' tube group) whose callback calls stepAllTracts unconditionally, with the registry size as the emptiness test. Then re-measure: stepAllTracts should run once per frame and the fade should take ~0.5 s.
findings.notes: Not a correctness bug in the target values (each step lerps toward the same per-instance target) — it is a doubled contract violation: the per-frame cost the refactor existed to remove is back, and the interaction animation the file documents is no longer an animation. Visible consequence is a single-frame pop on select/hover/syndrome dim instead of the documented lerp; there is no gate for either half.

findings.subject: budget-report.mjs — 'rendered triangles' counts the manifest only; the 149 procedural tubes add 214,560 tris and push the all-on scene 13,764 tris OVER the 800,000 cap the gate reports as PASS
findings.field: scripts/verify/budget-report.mjs (Σ parts[].triCount) vs SceneLayers.tsx:794-843 (TractTube instances)
findings.claimed: verify:budget-report prints '✓ rendered triangles 599,204 ≤ 800,000' and 'Σ parts[].triCount = 599,204 triangles'; README L280/L390 present this row as 'Rendered triangles (scene) | ≤ 800,000 | PASS'.
findings.expected: A gate labelled 'rendered triangles (scene)' counts every triangle the scene draws, or the row is labelled as the committed-mesh budget and the procedural tube families are counted in a separate row with their own cap.
findings.basis: Measured in this run. `npm run verify:budget-report` (exit 0): 'manifest: 138 part(s)', '✓ rendered triangles 599,204 ≤ 800,000', 'Σ parts[].triCount = 599,204'. The scene, however, also mounts one TractTube per visible course and one mirrored twin per paired course (SceneLayers.tsx:794-843). Built from the shipped tables: per tube = 803 vertices / 1,440 triangles (TUBULAR_SEGMENTS 72 × RADIAL_SEGMENTS 10 × 2, `buildTractGeometry`), 149 instances at all-on = 214,560 triangles. 599,204 + 214,560 = 813,764 > 800,000, i.e. 13,764 triangles (1.72%) over the cap in the all-on state, reachable in two clicks ('All areas on' + 'All systems on', Header.tsx:253/291). The default framing (brainstem-focus) mounts 70 tubes = 100,800 tris → 700,004 total, inside the cap, which is why the breach is invisible at boot. The tube families are also outside the gate's domain by construction (no manifest row, no GLB: README L571/L1347 'zero payload'), so no gate counts them.
findings.suggestedFix: Either add the procedural families to budget-report (import NERVE_COURSES/VESSEL_COURSES/tracts + the paired predicate, multiply by the shipped 1,440 tris/tube, print a separate 'procedural tubes' row and include it in the ≤800,000 verdict), or restate the README row as the committed-mesh budget and add an explicit tube row with its own cap. Do not change the tube tessellation silently: 72×10 is what the v2–v18 measurements were taken at.
findings.notes: Zero-payload procedural geometry is a documented, deliberate design (README L571) — the defect is the measurement, not the geometry. Related: rob-021 (the same two families are also absent from the worker registry's vessel half).

findings.subject: SectionCanvas.tsx:2121-2166 + sectionAssets.ts:285-339 — the 12 '#mirror' nerve contours are computed, transferred and thrown away; the 2D live section paints every paired cranial nerve on ONE side
findings.field: registryCourseParts `#mirror` slug suffix vs partsForCanvas() meta slugs in ensureRenderOrder (SectionCanvas.tsx:1219-1241)
findings.claimed: SceneLayers.tsx:816-825 and sectionAssets.ts:308-339 (v17): a paired nerve draws its twin on the other side; README v14 'the twelve nerves … both surfaces' and v17 'paired tracts/nerves mirrored on both sides'; verify:cranial-nerve-render and verify:area-toggles both assert 'every mirrored twin is the x → −x REFLECTION of its authored side (no cached duplicate)' and that the worker slices every registry part.
findings.expected: A contour returned by the worker for a mirrored twin is painted (and hit-tested) as a second instance of the same record on the other side, so the 2D surfaces show what the 3D surface shows; or the mirrored registry parts are not built at all.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction inside one feature. sectionAssets.ts:297 re-slugs the twin as `${mirrored.slug}#mirror`, so the worker returns contour entries keyed 'nrv-cn3-oculomotor#mirror'. SectionCanvas.tsx:1219 builds its draw list as `partsForCanvas().filter(meta => args.contours.has(meta.slug))`, and bitsForCanvas() emits SECTION_NERVE_PARTS/VESSEL_PARTS from NERVE_COURSES/VESSEL_COURSES — the AUTHORED ids only. Measured: registryNerveParts() = 24 parts (12 authored + 12 '#mirror', `nerve registry parts 24 mirror-suffixed 12`); partsForCanvas() = 191 metas; `mirror slugs matched by a canvas meta 0`. Hover/click use the same `cache.visibleFaces` list (SectionCanvas.tsx:2225-2232), so the twin is also unhoverable. Geometry proof that the discarded half is real work: authored `nrv-cn3-oculomotor` x ∈ [−0.494, 24.314], twin x ∈ [−24.314, 0.494] (y/z identical), and both slice at z=0 to 1 loop / 24 segments (1,440 triangles tested each). Cost: the twin half of the nerve registry is 0.308 MiB of the 0.616 MiB transferred, and 12 of 24 parts are re-sliced on every plane change for a result that is discarded. verify:area-toggles asserts the registry CONTENT (mirror present, reflected) but never asserts that a canvas meta can match a `#mirror` contour, which is why the gate is green.
findings.suggestedFix: In ensureRenderOrder (and the hit-test path), resolve a contour slug to its meta: `const meta = metaBySlug.get(slug.replace(/#mirror$/, ''))` with the twin drawn from the same meta but its own part (and, for selection/hover, the same `meta.group`), or give partsForCanvas() one meta per registry part (authored + `#mirror`) so the visible list and the worker registry are the same key space. Then extend verify:area-toggles to assert that every `#mirror` contour slug the worker returns matches exactly one canvas meta.
findings.notes: This is the 2D half of the v17 mirror claim; the 3D half is correct (SceneLayers.tsx:806/823/840 mount the mirrored TractTube, and the v18 blob retirement depends on it). Consequence is a visible left/right asymmetry in the Plates live section and in the 3D tab's simulated-section panel for all 12 cranial nerves — the surfaces disagree about laterality. Browser-pixel confirmation is orchestrator-only; the slug-space mismatch is provable in Node, which is what was measured here.

findings.subject: SectionCanvas.tsx:2097-2166 — registrySentRef latches after the first send, so the anatomy loader's retry can never reach the worker; after a successful retry the canvas under-renders while its loading banner disappears
findings.field: registrySentRef (line 1329/1371/2098/2135) + the init-registry effect deps [readyCount, total, workerError]
findings.claimed: anatomyAssets.ts:36-42 and Viewer3D.tsx:369-421: a slug that exceeded ANATOMY_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS settles to a visible 'geometry unavailable for N structures — the simplified shape is shown instead' notice with a Retry that re-runs the load ('geometry unavailable — retry'), i.e. the loader's failure state is recoverable. SectionCanvas.tsx:2114-2137 sends the worker registry once and the file's own P0 hand-off note (lines 1276-1299) treats the canvas banner as 'exactly the v5 one'.
findings.expected: After a retry resolves a timed-out slug, that slug's geometry reaches the contour worker (a second init message or an incremental add), so the 2D sections show the structures the notice said were being retried; the banner state and the painted content agree.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction between the loader's retry contract and the canvas' one-shot registry. `if (registrySentRef.current) return` (SectionCanvas.tsx:2098) is set to true on the first successful send (line 2135) and only reset when the worker effect re-runs (line 1371, i.e. on a SectionCanvas remount). The init effect's dependencies are numbers (`[geometryStatus.readyCount, geometryStatus.total, workerError]`), so a late geometry arrival changes readyCount but the effect returns at line 2098 without re-sending. Meanwhile `useSectionGeometryStatus()` (sectionAssets.ts:471-484) re-reads every `useAnatomyAsset`, so a recovered slug flips to 'ready' and `readyCount` reaches `total` — which is exactly the condition that STOPS the 'Loading anatomy meshes X/138…' overlay (SectionCanvas.tsx:1823-1832). Net effect: the canvas stops saying it is loading and paints without the recovered structures, with no visible signal. Recovery is possible only by unmounting the canvas (switching tabs) so the worker effect re-runs. The timeout itself is reachable by design (ANATOMY_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 15,000, anatomyAssets.ts:421) and `retryTimedOutAnatomyAssets()` is the documented affordance (Viewer3D.tsx:416).
findings.suggestedFix: Make the registry additive: keep a `sentSlugs` Set and, when a slug that was skipped (geometry null at send time) becomes ready, post a second `init` (or a new `{t:'add', parts}` message) with just that part, or clear registrySentRef when `geometryStatus.geometries` gains a slug it did not have at the last send (compare a signature, e.g. `readyCount` at last send vs now). Also finish the documented hand-off in the file's own note: expose `timedOutSlugs`/`retryGeometry()` from useSectionGeometryStatus so the Plates tab can offer the same Retry the 3D viewer has.
findings.notes: Severity major because the failure is silent-by-construction (a false 'everything loaded' state), not because it is frequent: it needs one 15 s stall. Measured the latch and the deps by reading the shipped effect; the reachable late-arrival path is the loader's own retry (`clearAnatomyAssetCache` + attempt bump).

findings.subject: anatomyAssets.ts:565-592 — a late-arriving stale parse DOES write into the geometry cache and DOES delete the newer in-flight entry, contradicting the file's own 'never leaks the timed-out attempt into the cache' contract
findings.field: loadAnatomyGeometry().then(...) — geometryCache.set(key, result) + inFlightLoads.delete(key) with no attempt guard
findings.claimed: anatomyAssets.ts:36-39: 'retry() drops the slug's cached url/in-flight entries and re-runs the load; it is safe to call from a button, is idempotent while a retry is already in flight, and never leaks the timed-out attempt into the cache (a late-arriving stale parse is ignored — the attempt counter below)'.
findings.expected: The abandoned attempt's completion is ignored for cache purposes: it must not overwrite `geometryCache[key]` produced by a newer attempt and must not delete a newer attempt's `inFlightLoads[key]` entry.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the file's own contract, and no attempt counter exists in the loader. The only 'attempt' state is `const [attempt, setAttempt] = useState(0)` in the hook (line 756), used only to re-run the effect; the module-level `loadAnatomyGeometry` has no generation guard: its settle handler runs `geometryCache.set(key, result); inFlightLoads.delete(key)` unconditionally (lines 580-581). Trace: attempt 1 stalls → the hook's timeout branch calls `clearAnatomyAssetCache(slug, mirrored)` (line 830), dropping url/in-flight/geometry for the key → a retry starts attempt 2, which registers `inFlightLoads.set(key, promise2)` (line 590) → attempt 1 finally resolves and (a) writes its geometry into the cache over attempt 2's, and (b) deletes promise2's in-flight registration, so a third concurrent consumer starts a THIRD parse instead of sharing. Consequence is bounded (the geometry is the same committed GLB, so no wrong pixels) but it is the exact leak the comment denies: a duplicated fetch/parse and a duplicated GPU geometry for one slug per timed-out-then-recovered part. No gate covers the loader's timeout/retry subsystem at all (grep over scripts/ for ANATOMY_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS, retryTimedOutAnatomyAssets, clearAnatomyAssetCache finds no consumer).
findings.suggestedFix: Give the loader an attempt generation: `const attempt = (attempts.get(key) ?? 0) + 1; attempts.set(key, attempt)` inside loadAnatomyGeometry, and in both settle handlers `if (attempts.get(key) !== attempt) return resultOrNull` before touching `geometryCache`/`inFlightLoads`. Then the stale attempt's value is still returned to its own awaiting hook (harmless) but cannot clobber the caches.
findings.notes: Also worth a gate: the whole P0 survivability subsystem (bounded loads, 'timedOut' state, retry) is currently untested by any script in scripts/ — it is asserted only in prose.

findings.subject: PipSection.tsx:137-141 — the 'no real imagery can arrive anyway' pixel guard is installed once at mount, so the canvas created by a failure-boundary Retry is unguarded
findings.field: useEffect(() => guardSimulatedOnlyCanvas(canvas), []) in PipSection (canvas resolved by containerRef.current.querySelector('canvas'))
findings.claimed: PipSection.tsx:24-33: 'The panel therefore resolves exactly the state item 4 introduces … 2. NO REAL IMAGERY CAN ARRIVE ANYWAY. The scope is a store write … So the canvas is ALSO guarded at the pixel chokepoint: every real-imagery paint path in section/imageLayers.ts ends in exactly two 2D calls — ctx.drawImage … and ctx.putImageData … and guardSimulatedOnlyCanvas shadows both on THIS canvas' context only, counting what it dropped.' A structural guarantee, not a convention.
findings.expected: Whichever canvas element the panel currently mounts is guarded: if SectionCanvas is remounted (the boundary's Retry, or any future key change), the guard is re-installed on the NEW canvas.
findings.basis: Code path: the guard effect has `[]` dependencies and captures the canvas ONCE via `containerRef.current?.querySelector('canvas')`. SectionErrorBoundary (SectionErrorBoundary.tsx:344-364, the shim the panel uses with name='Simulated section panel') renders the children again after `reset()`; PipSection itself is NOT remounted, so its effects do not re-run and the replacement `<canvas>` element is never shadowed. The primary defence (beginSectionPipImageryScope, PipSection.tsx:134, store.ts:1626+) does survive that remount, so the practical exposure is small — but the claim as written ('a guarantee that depends on a store write is only as strong as the next edit to the store, so the canvas is ALSO guarded') does not hold after the panel's own documented recovery path, and `pipSectionGuard.armed` would report 1 while the live canvas is unguarded. No gate can see this: verify:pip-contract tests the guard against a context double (pip-contract.mjs:390-410) and text-reads imageLayers.ts.
findings.suggestedFix: Re-resolve and re-guard the canvas after any subtree remount: give the guard effect a dependency that changes with the canvas (e.g. a callback ref on the canvas element, or a MutationObserver / a `resetKey` prop threaded from SectionCanvas), or mount the guard INSIDE SectionCanvas' own effect where the canvas ref is already known. Assert in pip-contract that remounting the guarded subtree re-arms the guard (call the reset path twice and check `armed` returns to 1).
findings.notes: Judged 'suspect' rather than 'wrong' because the store scope still holds in the measured path — the defect is the strength of the stated guarantee plus an incorrect diagnostic counter, not an observed pixel leak.

findings.subject: Worker error path: workerAliveRef=false with no restart and no retry affordance — a crashing contour worker freezes the section for the component's lifetime
findings.field: SectionCanvas.tsx:1376-1417 (onmessage 'error' / onerror / onmessageerror) + 1428/1455 (pumpPlane/postPlane early returns) + 2393-2395 (the failure note)
findings.claimed: QUALITY_PLAN §1 item 2 doctrine (restated in section/SectionErrorBoundary.tsx:6-11 and App.tsx:27-35): 'a failed surface must say so and offer recovery' — every other failure surface in this app pairs its message with an action (panel cards have Retry, the geometry notice has Retry, the context-loss overlay has Restore/Reload).
findings.expected: A worker-level failure either restarts the worker (terminate + new Worker + replay the registry) or shows a Retry control that does so; at minimum the section must not silently keep its last slice while refusing every later plane.
findings.basis: Code path, no gate. `workerAliveRef.current = false` is set on a worker 'error' message, on `worker.onerror` and on `worker.onmessageerror` (SectionCanvas.tsx:1379/1406/1411); `pumpPlane` returns immediately while it is false (1428) and `postPlane` refuses to post (1455), so the canvas keeps the last contours and the slider stops updating. Nothing re-creates the worker — the worker effect has `[]` deps and only runs on mount — and the rendered state is a passive note ('Contour worker failed: …', line 2394) with no button. The registry cannot be replayed to a new worker either (registrySentRef latch, rob-004). The user's only recovery is a tab switch/remount. grep over scripts/ finds no gate for this path (the §5 sweep's section-facing gates are verify:pipeline / verify:area-toggles / verify:cranial-nerve-*).
findings.suggestedFix: Add a 'Restart contour worker' button to the failure note that terminates the current worker, sets registrySentRef=false, creates a new Worker (extract the worker-construction + listener wiring into a callable so the effect and the retry share it) and re-sends the registry; or make the error path automatic (one silent restart, and only then the note). Assert in a Node gate that the restart path resets workerReadyRef/registrySentRef.
findings.notes: Severity minor because a worker 'error' message is rare (a throw inside computeSlice is caught and posted as {t:'error'}, which lands here) and the app stays interactive; the finding is about the missing recovery half of a stated doctrine and about the freeze being permanent for the lifetime of the component.

findings.subject: The SectionErrorBoundary's '?panelfail' production-safety claim names an assertion no gate performs, and the shipped bundle does contain the hook's strings
findings.field: SectionErrorBoundary.tsx:70-76 ('The hook cannot be reached in a shipped bundle even by hand-editing the URL — asserted by grepping the built bundle for panelfail')
findings.claimed: The dev-only forced-throw hook is unreachable in a production build, and that claim is verified by grepping the built bundle for `panelfail`.
findings.expected: Either the stated assertion exists (a gate that greps dist/assets/*.js and fails when the hook's arming path is live) or the sentence describes what was actually checked.
findings.basis: Measured on the committed build. dist/assets/index-DayLESCm.js contains the literal `panelfail` exactly once and the probe message 'audit probe: deliberate render failure' exactly once, together with the inlined env object (BASE_URL '/' , DEV !1, MODE 'production', PROD !0, SSR !1 — verbatim shape `{BASE_URL:'/',DEV:!1,MODE:'production',PROD:!0,SSR:!1}` in the bundle) and the guard that reads that object's DEV and returns '' before touching the URL, followed by the URLSearchParams(...).get('panelfail') read. So the DEFENCE is real and holds (DEV is statically false, so `panelFailTarget()` returns '' before the URL is read — the hook cannot be armed by hand-editing the URL), but the stated METHOD ('grepping the built bundle for panelfail') would FAIL as written (presence ≠ reachability), and no script performs it: the only dist-reading check is verify:a11y-contract.mjs:297-312, which reads the bundle for other reasons; grep over scripts/ for `panelfail` returns checks.mjs, audit.mjs, audit-checks.test.mjs, boundary-contract.mjs, closure-bite.mjs — none of which read dist/.

Do not assert absence of the string: the string is legitimately in the bundle.
findings.notes: Recorded as 'untested claim' per the run's rule that a claim with no gate is itself a finding. containment itself behaves correctly in the dev lane (verify:audit-checks.test.mjs §5 arms the Node seam and asserts exactly one probe; verify:boundary-contract.mjs exercises the card + Retry).

findings.subject: WebGL context loss: the documented v7/v9 contract is intact in the shipped source, and the v16–v18 diffs do not touch it
findings.field: Viewer3D.tsx:723-831 + 994-999 (overlay), 874-922 (CanvasSceneBoundary), PostFX.tsx:74-78, PipSection/SectionPiPPanel outside <Canvas>
findings.claimed: v7 closure gap 1/2: 'webglcontextlost → preventDefault → data-context-lost overlay with Restore/Reload; PostFX unmounted while lost; a throw in the canvas subtree is contained so the overlay survives; if no restore arrives within 20 s the overlay becomes terminal (data-context-lost="dead")'. v9 items 4+5: the simulated-section panel is DOM + a 2D canvas outside the R3F canvas, so it cannot be taken down by a GL loss.
findings.expected: Those paths are present and cannot be reached by the v16–v18 selection/material/vessel changes.
findings.basis: Source + git evidence. Listeners are attached to the canvas element in an effect that runs before the first frame (callback ref, Viewer3D.tsx:732/785-811); `onLost` calls event.preventDefault() (mandatory for the browser to ever fire webglcontextrestored); the 20 s terminal timer is CONTEXT_LOSS_DEAD_MS (line 213, effect at 819-823); the restore path re-applies resetState + localClippingEnabled + ACES + sRGB + applyClipState and bumps envGeneration/sceneGeneration (772-803); PostFX returns null while `contextLost` (PostFX.tsx:78) so the measured `getContextAttributes().alpha` TypeError cannot re-occur; CanvasSceneBoundary (fallback null, THREE-safe) wraps the env, the scene and the post stack, and reports into a DOM notice (CanvasSceneFailureNotice). The panel is a sibling of `<Canvas>` (Viewer3D.tsx:943 closes the Canvas, 953 mounts SectionPiPPanel) and verify:pip-contract asserts the DOM order (pip-contract.mjs:1279-1285: `.viewer3d-canvas` offset < `<SectionPiPPanel` offset) and renders the panel with react-dom/server — i.e. the panel is provably a DOM tree, not an R3F subtree. `git show --stat` for the v16/v16b/v16d/v17/v18/v18b commits (51b6bee, 805b5f6, fd7c9f6, 84c666b, 54d75a1, 8d80572) shows they touch only SectionCanvas.tsx, store.ts, SceneLayers.tsx, TractTube.tsx, sectionAssets.ts, vasculature-courses.ts, anatomyAssets.ts — none of Viewer3D's context-loss code path. verify:closure-bite.mjs bite #? removes `data-context-lost={phase}` and asserts a FAIL, so the attribute is gate-protected.

findings.subject: CanvasContextRecovery: the frameloop token is written into the R3F root state and never cleaned up — safe only because the R3F root unmounts with Viewer3D
findings.field: Viewer3D.tsx:285-313 (state.setFrameloop('never'|'always'))
findings.claimed: The frame loop is frozen while the context is gone so three cannot walk the scene graph with no context, and restored afterwards; 'restoring always is always correct' (lines 278-283).
findings.expected: Unmounting Viewer3D while the context is lost must not leave a global frame-loop state behind that a later mount inherits.

findings.notes: Recorded as a checked item of the brief (context-loss survival), not as a defect.

findings.subject: Disposal inventory: every per-instance material has a matching dispose; R3F does NOT dispose prop-passed geometry/material, so the shared module-level caches are safe (measured against the installed @react-three/fiber 8.17.10)
findings.field: NucleusMesh.tsx:164-168, TractTube.tsx:423-446, PlaneHelpers.tsx:243-273 (dispose={null}), Viewer3D.tsx:189-201 (PMREM/RoomEnvironment), SceneLayers.tsx:303-310/375-377 + SomatotopyOverlay.tsx:85-90 (module singletons)
findings.claimed: NucleusMesh.tsx:158-161 and TractTube.tsx:421-422 both state 'three re-acquires disposed materials, so the StrictMode setup→cleanup→setup cycle is safe'; PlaneHelpers.tsx:262-265 states the module-scoped grid geometry must not be freed by R3F (`dispose={null}`) because 'the guarantee THREE.GridHelper.dispose() destroys'.
findings.expected: Per-instance materials are released on unmount; shared/cached geometry and module singletons are NOT released by an unrelated unmount; declaratively-created (JSX-child) resources ARE released.
findings.basis: Read from the installed renderer, not assumed. @react-three/fiber 8.17.10 (dist/events-321b05fb.esm.js): `removeRecursive(child.__r3f?.objects, child, shouldDispose)` and `removeRecursive(child.children, ...)` then `if (shouldDispose && child.dispose && child.type !== 'Scene') child.dispose()` (lines 152-177) — it walks only DECLARATIVELY attached objects, and `applyProps` assigns prop values directly (`currentInstance[key] = value`, line 747). A THREE.Mesh has no `dispose` method in three 0.169 (grep of three.module.js: no dispose in the Mesh class body). Therefore prop-passed geometry/material are never auto-disposed, which is exactly what the shared caches need; the explicit `useEffect(() => () => material.dispose(), [material])` in NucleusMesh/TractTube is the only disposal of those materials and covers unmount. PlaneHelpers relies on the opposite behaviour for its JSX children (`<planeGeometry>`/`<meshBasicMaterial>` are R3F-owned → disposed) and explicitly sets `dispose={null}` on the module-scoped line grid. SceneEnvironment disposes renderTarget + RoomEnvironment + PMREMGenerator in its cleanup (Viewer3D.tsx:195-200). Module singletons that are deliberately app-lifetime and never disposed: SHARED_NUCLEUS_GEOMETRY (NucleusMesh.tsx:37), the 10 ENVELOPE_MATERIALS + 10 ENVELOPE_SLOTS geometries (SceneLayers.tsx:356-377), 2 ghost-shell materials (303-310), 16 somatotopy PATCH_MATERIALS + 1 patch disc (SomatotopyOverlay.tsx:79-90), the 3 plane-helper sheets (PlaneHelpers.tsx:220-234), the striation DataTexture + its ≤5 clones (textures.ts:108, TractTube.tsx:259-270), the ventricle geometry cache (SceneLayers.tsx:397-408).
findings.suggestedFix: None. The one asymmetry worth a comment is that the module singletons are only protected by the prop-passing rule — a future edit that turns one of them into a JSX child (`<meshPhysicalMaterial …/>`) would make R3F dispose it on the first layer toggle.
findings.notes: Measured by reading the installed bundle and three build, not by trusting the comments — this was the single largest 'does it leak?' question in the brief.

findings.subject: Module-level geometry caches hold 6.25 MiB at all-on (2.94 MiB at the default framing) and are never evicted — bounded by construction, but the tube cache accepts an arbitrary caller key
findings.field: TractTube.tsx:107 tubeCache (keyed by cacheKey), sectionAssets.ts:316-374 (registryCourseParts callers), anatomyAssets.ts:521 geometryCache
findings.claimed: TractTube.tsx:106 'Tube geometries are cached module-level so layer toggles never rebuild' and 226-231 'The cache is keyed on the record id, so twelve nerve courses add twelve entries and a layer toggle never re-sweeps anything'; anatomyAssets.ts:54-59 'Cache lifetime = app lifetime (module singletons, StrictMode-safe) … they are intentionally never disposed'.
findings.expected: The caches are bounded by the shipped authoring tables, so a session cannot grow them without bound; a layer toggle re-uses geometry instead of re-sweeping.
findings.basis: Measured through the shipped builder + cache: 149 distinct keys at all-on (46 tract-instance keys, 24 nerve, 79 vessel), holding 6.248 MiB of CPU-side attribute/index data and 214,560 triangles (tract 1.929 MiB / nerve 1.006 MiB / vessel 3.313 MiB; 52.6 kB per tube: 803 verts × (12+12+12+8 B) + 4,320 × 4 B index). At the default framing (brainstem-focus: vasculature region off) only 70 keys / 2.935 MiB are ever built. Every key is derived from a course/record id in a committed table (23 tracts, 12 nerves, 41 vessel courses) plus the `#mirror` suffix, so the cache is finite: max 152 keys. `tubeGeometryFor(record, cacheKey = record.id)` does expose the key, so a future caller could mint unbounded entries — the only current callers are TractTube (id / id#mirror) and sectionAssets (id / id#mirror), both finite.
findings.suggestedFix: None required. If the mirror/segment families grow, consider an LRU bound (or a dev-only assertion that tubeCache.size ≤ the authored course count × 2) so the 'bounded by the tables' property is enforced rather than implied.
findings.notes: Judged ok: the memory is real but small, deliberate, and re-used across every layer toggle — the point of the cache.

findings.subject: clearAnatomyAssetCache() drops cached BufferGeometry references without disposing them — a recovered slug can end up with two GPU-resident geometries
findings.field: anatomyAssets.ts:601-613 (clearAnatomyAssetCache) called from the hook's timeout branch (830) and from retry() (773) and retryTimedOutAnatomyAssets() (730)
findings.claimed: anatomyAssets.ts:596-600: 'Safe to call at any time; the previously handed-out BufferGeometry objects keep rendering (they are owned by the scene until it is rebuilt), so this never blanks a live frame.'
findings.expected: Geometry a consumer may still be drawing keeps rendering (true, and the comment says so), but geometry nobody references is released with BufferGeometry.dispose() so its GL buffers are freed — otherwise a retry cycle allocates a second geometry for the same slug.
findings.basis: Code path + three.js ownership rule. geometryCache entries are dropped by `geometryCache.delete(key)` (lines 610-611) with no dispose call anywhere in the module (grep: anatomyAssets.ts contains no `.dispose(`). On the timeout path the mesh that was drawing the old geometry is still mounted (NucleusMesh holds `asset.geometry` in its state) and the loader's stale attempt writes a NEW geometry for the same key (rob-005), so after a retry there can be two BufferGeometry objects for one slug, the abandoned one still referenced by a hook state that React will eventually drop. three.js's documented ownership rule is that BufferGeometry.dispose() must be called when the geometry is no longer used (three.js docs, 'How to dispose of objects'); the module's own contract is a deliberate deviation for HANDED-OUT geometry, but it does not distinguish 'handed out' from 'produced by an abandoned attempt'. Cost is bounded by the number of retried slugs (a timed-out-then-recovered slug = +52 kB…+1.4 MiB CPU + GPU).
findings.suggestedFix: Track handed-out geometries separately (e.g. a `delivered: Set<BufferGeometry>`), and dispose only those cache evictions that were never handed to a consumer; or, simpler, do not let an abandoned attempt write into the cache at all (rob-005) — then a clear() only ever drops objects nobody holds and can dispose safely.
findings.notes: Judged suspect rather than wrong: the visible behaviour is correct and the leak is bounded; the basis is the library's ownership rule plus the module's own inability to tell the two cases apart.

findings.subject: Contour worker protocol under rapid plane changes: the 15 Hz / 0.25 au contract is implemented on both sides, and one slice is ~10× inside the 15 Hz budget (measured)
findings.field: SectionCanvas.tsx:204-208/1423-1462 (quantizePlane + POST_INTERVAL_MS + pending/in-flight coalescing) and contourWorker.ts:112-193 (CACHE_MAX 24, `desired` single-slot coalescing, computing guard)
findings.claimed: SectionCanvas header (96-104): 'plane updates are quantized to 0.25 au and posted at ≤ 15 Hz while dragging (trailing ack keeps the newest plane); contour extraction happens ONLY in the worker … the worker result cache + bbox cull keep slicing cheap'. contourWorker.ts:12-17: 'a plane update arriving while a slice is running replaces the queued job … an LRU result cache (24 planes) makes slider scrubbing back and forth instantaneous'.
findings.expected: No unbounded queue, no stale result painted over a newer plane, and a slice that fits the 66.7 ms 15 Hz window with margin.
findings.basis: Measured + code. Main thread: PLANE_QUANTIZE_STEP = 0.25 and POST_INTERVAL_MS = 1000/15 = 66.67 ms; `pumpPlane()` keeps a single `pendingRef` slot, refuses to post while `inFlightRef` is set (the ack re-pumps), and arms exactly one `postTimerRef` window timer, cleared on unmount (line 2336). Worker: one `desired` slot (newest wins), `computing` guard, try/catch → `{t:'error'}` with `computing=false; desired=null` so the queue cannot wedge, and a 24-entry result cache. Slice cost measured by running the SHIPPED contours module over the registry the canvas actually sends (138 GLB parts + 24 nerve parts = 162): mean 3.6 ms, worst 6.9 ms over a 76-plane transverse sweep (−60…+90 au at 2 au steps) — 9.7× inside the 66.7 ms budget (single planes: 3.9–12.3 ms depending on the cut; the 12.3 ms figure is first-call JIT). The related gate prints the same order of magnitude: `npm run verify:pipeline` (exit 0) reports 2–9 ms per plane for the 138 GLB parts over 13 planes with heap 11–20 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: None. Note for the integrator: because vessel contours are never sent (rob-021) and mirrored nerve contours are discarded (rob-003), the worker currently spends 12 of every 24 nerve parts' worth of slicing on a result the canvas cannot use — fixing how the canvas consumes `#mirror` slugs would also make that work visible, and fixing rob-021 would roughly double the per-plane triangle count (still inside budget: +79 vessel parts).
findings.notes: The budget statement excludes transfer/serialisation cost, which is one-shot (init), not per plane.

findings.subject: Transferable ownership: the worker registry is built from FRESH copies, so the 3D scene's cached GLB attributes can never be detached; the DataCloneError fallback is real but untested
findings.field: sectionAssets.ts:409-453 registryPartFromGeometry, SectionCanvas.tsx:2138-2164 (transfer list + structured-clone fallback)
findings.claimed: sectionAssets.ts:12-16: 'Positions/indices are COPIED out for the worker: the parsed BufferGeometries back the 3D scene and must never have their attributes detached by transfer'; SectionCanvas.tsx:2145-2148: 'The arrays stay intact on failure, so retry as a structured clone'.
findings.expected: Transferring the registry must not detach any ArrayBuffer a mounted mesh is drawing; a rejected transfer must fall back to a clone and still deliver the registry.
findings.basis: Code + measurement. registryPartFromGeometry allocates `new Float32Array(position.count * 3)` and `new Uint32Array(sourceIndex.count)` — always fresh buffers, with an accessor fallback for unpacked layouts — so `worker.postMessage(init, [positions…, indices…])` (276 transfer entries for 138 parts) can only detach copies. The GLB path is the same adapter (SectionCanvas.tsx:2115-2120 → registryPartFromGeometry(meta, geometry)), and the procedural families go through it too (sectionAssets.ts:322/332/364/368). Measured payload per init: GLB family 10.28 MiB (3.42 MiB of Float32 positions from 298,734 glTF vertices + 6.86 MiB of Uint32 indices from 1,797,612 indices) + the 24 nerve parts 0.616 MiB = 10.90 MiB allocated and copied on the main thread at first send. Because the copies are fresh per call, a remount re-sends fresh arrays (measured: 103 unique slugs over both families, 0 collisions) — there is no detached-buffer re-mount hazard. The structured-clone fallback path itself has no gate: verify:area-toggles and verify:pipeline exercise `extractContours` directly and never construct a Worker, so 'a DataCloneError is survivable' is asserted in prose only.
findings.suggestedFix: None for the ownership contract. If the integrator wants the fallback covered, a Node test can post the same message through `node:worker_threads` with a deliberately non-transferable entry (e.g. a plain Array of numbers) and assert the second postMessage still delivers 138 parts.
findings.notes: The main-thread cost of the initial copy (~10.9 MiB, one pass over 138 geometries) is real but one-shot per canvas mount; there is exactly one SectionCanvas mounted at a time (App.tsx mounts tabs exclusively), so one worker and one copy exist at any moment.

findings.subject: No double-register or leak on SectionCanvas re-mount: one worker per mount, terminated on unmount, registry rebuilt from scratch; the init-registry effect is idempotent under StrictMode
findings.field: SectionCanvas.tsx:1368-1419 (worker effect, cleanup terminate) + 2097-2166 (init effect, registrySentRef) + 2327-2348 (unmount cleanup: rAF, timers, Path2D cache)
findings.claimed: contourWorker.ts:17-18: 'the worker is terminated on SectionCanvas unmount (no leaks while the authored-plate view is open)'; SectionCanvas.tsx:1369-1371 spells out the StrictMode remount handshake.
findings.expected: Mounting the canvas twice (StrictMode) or toggling tabs does not leave a second live worker, a duplicated registry or a stale rAF loop.
findings.basis: Code path, plus the exclusivity measurement. The worker effect resets `registrySentRef`/`workerReadyRef` at mount, creates exactly one Worker in the effect body and calls `worker.terminate()` in the cleanup, so StrictMode's setup→cleanup→setup leaves one live worker; the init effect is guarded by `registrySentRef` and re-armed by the same mount reset; the unmount effect cancels the pending rAF, clears the 15 Hz window timer and empties the render-order cache (paths/bytes/visible lists/key). Registration is slug-keyed and the slugs are unique across both procedural families (measured 103 slugs / 103 unique), so a re-mount cannot double-register a part inside one worker. Only one SectionCanvas exists at a time: App.tsx renders the 3D tab (which contains the PiP panel's SectionCanvas via PipSection) OR the Plates tab, never both (App.tsx:214-228), so the 10.9 MiB registry is never duplicated across two live workers.
findings.suggestedFix: None. The one residual risk is the tab-exclusivity itself: if a future change keeps both tabs mounted (e.g. hidden instead of unmounted), two workers × 10.9 MiB registries would exist — worth an assertion in verify:pip-contract or a comment at the App tab switch.
findings.notes: Checked as a brief item ('do the section registry parts leak or double-register on re-mount?'). Verified statically plus by the uniqueness measurement; the Worker API itself cannot be exercised in this sandbox.

findings.subject: GLB parse/resolve failures degrade exactly as documented: missing slug → immediate fallback, parse rejection → catch → retryable on the next mount
findings.field: anatomyAssets.ts:503-518 (firstMeshGeometry), 565-592 (catch → inFlightLoads.delete → null), 807-857 (effect + status transitions)
findings.claimed: anatomyAssets.ts:17-21: 'useAnatomyPart / useAnatomyAsset hooks degrade gracefully: a slug that is missing from the manifest, has no GLB on disk, fails to parse, or does not resolve inside ANATOMY_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS reports status fallback and the caller renders the v1 primitive — the app never blanks (REALISM_PLAN §2 constraint 6)'.
findings.expected: Each failure class lands in a terminal, visible state that still draws something and can be retried.
findings.basis: Code path. Unknown slug → `partBySlug.get(slug) === undefined` → lazy initial FALLBACK_ASSET and an effect that returns without fetching (lines 763-769, 808-811). Known slug whose eager-false glob entry is missing → loadGlbUrl resolves null. Fetch/parse rejection → `loadAnatomyGeometry` catches, drops the in-flight entry (so a later mount retries) and resolves null → `fallbackAsset(part, false, retry)`. Geometry with no mesh node → firstMeshGeometry returns null → same path. Timeout → clearAnatomyAssetCache + timedOutKeys.add + `{status:'fallback', timedOut:true}` and the app-wide notice with Retry (Viewer3D.tsx:380-422). Measured census of the drawn scene at all-on: 240 records pass isStructureVisible, 133 of them resolve no committed GLB for any of their own slugs and therefore render the v1 ellipsoid — all 133 carry origin3d/size3d (0 exceptions), so none lands as a unit sphere at the world origin (the v7/C10 defect class).
findings.suggestedFix: None. (The fallback bodies are a documented schematic-placement decision, not a failure; the failure classes above are what this finding is about.)
findings.notes: The 133 fallback records are why the geometry-unavailable NOTICE matters: a timed-out slug looks identical to a deliberately schematic one, which is what makes rob-004's silent under-render the important half.

findings.subject: Imaging loader is bounded end to end: grid fetch has AbortController + 15 s deadline + first-class 'timeout' state + retry; plate decodes have their own 15 s deadline; the slice cache is byte-budgeted
findings.field: imageLayers.ts:807 (PLATE_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS), 840-848 (retryPlateImage), 1095 (GRID_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS), 1156-1171 (retryGridLoad), 1186-1277 (loadGrid), 1401-1436 (slice cache budget)
findings.claimed: QUALITY_PLAN §1 item 3 / AUDIT §2.3 as restated in the file: 'every plate decode is bounded … a timed-out plate is a DIFFERENT state (could not be loaded, not still arriving), and the retry affordance below is what makes it recoverable'; for the grids, 'the request is bounded by timeoutMs. On expiry the controller aborts the fetch and the entry settles to status timeout (visible + retryable) instead of staying loading forever'; the slice cache holds '24 MB, i.e. ≈13 MRI slices … with a counted budget'.
findings.expected: No unbounded wait, no unbounded cache, and a retry path for each failure.
findings.basis: Code path. Plate images: one `` + one 15 s timer per manifest id (`stainImageTimers`), on load/error the timer is cleared, on expiry the id enters `stainImageTimedOut` (a state distinct from `stainImageFailed`) and the state is readable via plateLoadState(); retryPlateImage() clears image/failed/timed-out and nudges a repaint. Grids: entry {status, grid, fetch, controller, timedOut}; the deadline arms a setTimeout that sets timedOut and aborts the controller; the catch distinguishes abort (status 'timeout', timedOut true, console warning) from a real rejection (status 'failed' + gridLoadError message); every terminal path nulls `entry.fetch` so a retry starts a fresh attempt; retryGridLoad refuses while a non-timed-out attempt is live; payload integrity is checked (manifest dims/origin/spacing shape + `buffer.byteLength !== dims[0]*dims[1]*dims[2]`). Slice cache: charged `w*h*4` per entry with oldest-first eviction to a 24 MiB budget and an explicit single-entry-over-budget rule. No gate covers the timer paths (verify-imaging-v4/-v4b read the module as TEXT for tolerance/fit invariants; audit-checks imports ctCoverageStatement), so the bounded-load behaviour itself is asserted in prose.
findings.suggestedFix: None required for behaviour. If the integrator wants coverage, a Node test can call loadGrid's exported retry surface with a stub fetch that never settles plus a small timeoutMs and assert the entry reaches 'timeout' (the function signature already accepts timeoutMs).
findings.notes: One honest limit, documented in the file: an `` request cannot be aborted, so a timed-out plate leaves its network request open until the browser finishes it — the STATE is terminal and retryable, the socket is not cancellable.

findings.subject: 'no real imagery at this plane' is an honest, coded fallback on both 2D surfaces (no-anchor / beyond-source / unavailable / loading), and the CT coverage limit is stated from one function

Gates: verify-imaging-v4.mjs and verify-imaging-v4b.mjs assert the tolerance/manifest invariants and the shipped statement text; verify:audit-checks imports ctCoverageStatement and asserts the apex sentence; the browser confirmation (that the text really appears at that plane) is orchestrator-only.

findings.subject: The vessel course family never reaches the contour worker: SectionCanvas appends only registryNerveParts(), so 79 registry parts (2.08 MiB of copies) are built, proven and dropped (the v17 open handoff)
findings.field: SectionCanvas.tsx:2126 `registryParts.push(...registryNerveParts())` vs sectionAssets.ts:361-382 (registryVesselParts / registryCoursePartsAll) and SectionCanvas.tsx:1219 (partsForCanvas carries 41 vessel metas)

Measured on the shipped modules: registryVesselParts() = 79 parts (41 authored + 38 mirrored) whose positions+indices total 2.08 MiB of fresh typed arrays per call, and SECTION_VESSEL_PARTS = 41 metas already in partsForCanvas() (191 metas). Consequence: the artery courses the user sees in 3D (v17's headline feature, and the fix for the retired lenticulostriate blobs) are absent from the Plates live section and from the 3D tab's simulated-section panel; the contours that would paint them exist and are one line away. Do not leave both halves as they are.
findings.notes: The brief asked whether the procedural nerve + vessel parts leak or double-register on re-mount: they do neither (rob-017) — the defect is that the vessel half is never sent at all.

findings.subject: localStorage: all six neuroaxis.* keys have validated, total read paths and try/caught writes; corrupt, legacy and hostile payloads degrade to defaults
findings.claimed: Each key's own comment: quality and viewPreset 'a stored value is validated against the preset table, so a stale/corrupt key falls back to the default instead of throwing'; sectionUnderlay 'Persisted settings win field by field … malformed JSON — use defaults' plus the v16 opacity migration; sectionLobes 'anything else (absent, corrupt, storage disabled) is OFF'; sectionPipSize 'clamped on read … a stored value is user-writable: a missing field, a string, NaN, a 10 000 px box or malformed JSON must all resolve to a usable size'; sectionPip 'Persisted value wins; default is VISIBLE'.
findings.expected: A hand-edited, truncated, wrong-typed or legacy payload never throws, never yields NaN/Infinity geometry, and never leaves a control in an unrenderable state.
findings.basis: Code path per key. quality: only 'high'|'balanced' accepted, else device detection, all inside try/catch (store.ts:86-96). viewPreset: `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(VIEW_PRESETS, stored)` (796-808) so an unknown string cannot become a preset. sectionUnderlay: JSON.parse + object test inside try/catch; kind via isUnderlayKind, opacity/windowMin/windowMax via isFiniteNumber, realFirst via typeof boolean, ctWindowPreset via isCtWindowPreset; the v3 payload (no schemaVersion) is migrated and a legacy below-1 opacity is lifted to the current default (v16 migration, 403-423); writes stamp schemaVersion 2. sectionLobes: strict '1'/'0' (451-462). sectionPipSize: clampSectionPipSize is total over unknown/NaN/Infinity/negative/non-integer input (299-314) and is applied on read (480-495) and on every drag frame. sectionPip: strict 'visible'/'hidden' (166-177). Every writer wraps setItem in try/catch, so private mode degrades to session-only. The format/kind migrations are also the only place the store accepts an externally-authored shape, and both are exercised by shipped gates (store load-time assertions; pip-contract renders the panel).
findings.suggestedFix: None for the six keys as such. See rob-023 for the two unclamped NUMERIC fields inside sectionUnderlay (windowMin/windowMax) and rob-024 for the stale viewPreset write path.
findings.notes: Also verified: nothing in src/ writes a `neuroaxis.*` key outside these six (grep over src/ returns only these constants and their comments), so there is no undocumented storage surface.

findings.subject: sectionUnderlay.windowMin/windowMax are the only persisted numbers with no range or ordering clamp — a corrupt payload paints a constant (all-black or all-white) base plate
findings.field: store.ts:419-420 (read) and 1582-1583 (setSectionUnderlay merge); consumer imageLayers.ts:1443-1446 windowMap
findings.claimed: store.ts:296-298 states the clamping rule for the sibling key ('a user-writable value … applied on READ from localStorage as well as on every drag frame'), and the same file's defaultValue doc (355-362) presents windowMin/windowMax as a window 'in uint8'.
findings.expected: A persisted window is either validated into a sane uint8 range with min < max, or the consumer treats an inverted/out-of-range window as 'no valid window' and keeps the previous/default value — never as a silently constant raster.
findings.basis: Code path. `if (isFiniteNumber(record.windowMin)) next.windowMin = record.windowMin` (419-420) accepts any finite number: 1e9, −1e9, or windowMin > windowMax. The merge in setSectionUnderlay is the same (1582-1583). The consumer's `windowMap(sample, wMin, wMax)` is `wMax > wMin ? clamp01((sample-wMin)/(wMax-wMin))*255 : (sample >= wMax ? 255 : 0)` (1443-1446) — deliberately total (no NaN), but for an inverted or absurd window it returns a constant: e.g. windowMin = 1e9 → every sample < 1e9 → 0 → a fully BLACK plate drawn over the section as the 'real' MRI/CT base, with the credit line claiming a modality is shown. That is the opposite of the loader's stated style everywhere else ('the app never blanks', 'a plane with no real imagery says so'). No gate covers the window fields (verify-imaging-v4/v4b read tolerance/fit invariants).
findings.suggestedFix: Clamp on read and on write: `next.windowMin = clampInt(record.windowMin, 0, 255)`, same for max, and if `max <= min` fall back to the defaults (or swap). One helper next to clampSectionPipSize, applied in both places, keeps the 'user-writable value is clamped on read' rule uniform across the storage keys.
findings.notes: Judged suspect: it needs a hostile or corrupted payload (the UI sliders cannot produce it), the failure is graceful in the crash sense (no exception, no NaN), and the visible result is a wrong-but-rendered plate.

findings.subject: neuroaxis.viewPreset is written by exactly ONE control (the Clinical motor button) but read at every boot — a legacy value keeps overriding the user's v12 area/system toggles on reload
findings.field: store.ts:1533-1545 (applyViewPreset is the only writer) + 796-808 (initialLayers restores it wholesale); Header.tsx:414 (the only call site)
findings.claimed: Header.tsx:51-58: 'Reset calls the store's EXISTING applyViewPreset("brainstem-focus") … All likewise resolves through VIEW_PRESETS.all (via ALL_ON_LAYERS), the neuroaxis.viewPreset write included, so a returning visitor keeps the framing they chose exactly as clicking a preset always did.' store.ts:56-60: the preset 'is a user preference, not a session value, so a returning visitor gets their own framing back'.
findings.expected: Every layer-changing control that can produce a persisted framing either writes the key or the key is not applied at boot; and a key whose domain the current UI cannot express should not silently drive the boot state.
findings.basis: Code path. The v12 header removed the preset row (Header.tsx:74-84), and `applyViewPreset` — the only writer of `neuroaxis.viewPreset` (store.ts:1539) — now has a single call site, the Clinical motor button (Header.tsx:414). The All modules and every area/system button go through `setSlice`→`toggleRegionLayer`/`toggleKindLayer` (Header.tsx:164-198), which never touch the key. `initialLayers()` (796-808) applies a valid persisted preset WHOLESALE at boot. Consequences: (a) a user who last used the v7–v11 preset row keeps booting into that framing, and no v12+ control states or updates it unless they click Clinical motor twice; (b) any manual area/system combination a user builds (up to two clicks to 'all on') is session-only and is silently replaced by the stale preset on the next reload — the header's 'a returning visitor keeps the framing they chose' is true only for preset clicks. The docstring lines that describe a Reset button and an all-on preset write (Header.tsx:3, 51-58) are themselves stale prose (no Reset button is rendered: grep of the JSX finds none).
findings.suggestedFix: Decide one policy and state it: either clear the key whenever an individual area/system toggle runs (`localStorage.removeItem(VIEW_PRESET_STORAGE_KEY)` in toggleRegionLayer/toggleKindLayer, with a comment) or persist the layer sets themselves (regions/kinds/hidden) as the v11 one-decision model would suggest. Either way, update the stale Header docstring and let a gate assert the chosen policy (e.g. that no persisted key can put the header into a state no visible control can reach).
findings.notes: Judged suspect rather than wrong: nothing crashes and the behaviour is arguably 'last explicit preset wins', but the key is now unreachable for most of its domain, which is exactly the kind of stale-persistence hazard the brief's item (5) asks about.

findings.subject: Empty layer state ('All off'): 0 structures, 0 tubes, 0 envelopes, no ghost shell — verified safe, but nothing in the app says the scene is empty
findings.field: Header 'All areas off' + 'All systems off' → layers.regions/kinds empty; SceneLayers.tsx:165-272 predicates; SectionCanvas visible list
findings.claimed: The toggle rows document their action ('All areas off — hide every area', 'All systems off — remove every structure system'), and the app's own doctrine elsewhere is that a blank or degraded surface must say so (SectionCanvas draws 'Loading anatomy meshes X/138…' rather than nothing; Viewer3D draws the geometry-unavailable notice and the imagery hint; the panel boundaries render failure cards).
findings.expected: With every layer off, the 3D pane and the section canvas state that every layer is off (and that this is a choice), rather than presenting an empty black frame as if it were the model.
findings.basis: Measured + grep. Executing the shipped predicates with empty sets: isStructureVisible → 0 of 264 records, isTractVisible → 0 of 23 tracts (so 0 of 149 tubes), isEnvelopeSlotVisible → 0 of 10 slots, isGhostShellVisible → false (no hemisphere outline), viewPresetOf(empty) → null (so the Clinical motor button correctly reports itself unpressed). The 2D canvas then has an empty draw list and paints background + grid + crosshair + readout only. A grep of src/ for empty-state copy ('nothing is visible', 'all layers are off', 'no structures', …) returns no match: the only state-dependent notices are the loading banner (readyCount < total) and the imagery hint. The Legend's per-region/per-kind checkboxes do show the off state, and the header's All-off buttons are unpressed — so the state is discoverable in the controls, not in the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Draw the same class of notice the canvas already owns: when the visible-part list and the 3D admission are both empty AND the layer sets are empty, paint 'every area and system is off — use All on in the header' in the 3D overlay (next to the existing hints) and/or in the section canvas' overlay slot. Both surfaces already have the exact DOM/canvas slots for it (viewer-hint paragraph; section-overlay-note).
findings.notes: Judged suspect with a judgment basis: it is a discoverability/robustness-of-communication gap, not a crash. Two clicks ('All areas off' + 'All systems off') reach it, and one click ('All areas on') leaves the systems still off, so the empty state is easy to land in.

findings.subject: Rapid Areas/Systems toggling is order-independent and batched: one fresh Set per store write, ≤7 writes per click, React 18 batches them, draws are rAF-coalesced
findings.field: Header.tsx:164-198 (toggleArea/setSlice) + store.ts:1505-1519 (toggleRegionLayer/toggleKindLayer) + SectionCanvas.tsx:2307 (store subscribe → scheduleDraw)
findings.claimed: Header.tsx:158-163: 'one store write per region of the area whose layer state differs from the target, so the row and the per-region checkboxes the Legend and the taxonomy tree read can never disagree'; SceneLayers.tsx:163 'Pure and total: no store access, no geometry, no allocation'; SectionCanvas.tsx:1473-1501 'draws are rAF-coalesced'.
findings.expected: Hammering the rows cannot interleave into an inconsistent layer state, cannot leak registrations, and cannot queue unbounded redraws.
findings.basis: Code path. Each toggle is a pure functional update of one flag inside a NEW Set (store.ts:1507-1518), so no update depends on another's result and any interleaving converges to the same set; `setSlice` issues at most 7 writes (7 regions, 7 kinds) and React 18 batches them inside the click handler into one re-render. Consumers are memoized on the layer-set identities (SceneLayers.tsx:624-676: layerSets, visibleStructures, visibleTracts, visibleNerveCourses, visibleVesselCourses), so a burst of writes costs one filter pass per axis per render, and the meshes are keyed by slug/record so React reuses the instances instead of remounting them. The 2D surface subscribes to the store and calls scheduleDraw (SectionCanvas.tsx:2307), which is a single rAF latch, and the plane pump coalesces to one pending plane (rob-015). No registrations exist on the toggle path at all (only the worker registry, which is mount-scoped), so toggle bursts cannot leak.
findings.suggestedFix: None. If a future control needs to write both axes, prefer a single store action over the ≤7-write loop — the loop is correct but it is N notifications where one would do.
findings.notes: Checked as a brief item ('rapid toggling of Areas/Systems rows'). The one measurable cost of a burst is the full SceneLayers re-render of 442 body meshes + 149 tubes per layer-set change; the budget for that is rob-002/rob-029.

findings.subject: Selecting a structure whose mesh failed to load, and a record with no origin3d: the v1 primitive is drawn and pickable, no NaN anchors, and no record reaches the world origin as a 1 au ball
findings.field: NucleusMesh.tsx:175-205 (anchor/scale/label fallbacks) + curves.ts:34-38 (explodeDirection) + anatomyAssets.TEL_CONTENT_ONLY_IDS / isGhostOrContentOnly
findings.claimed: NucleusMesh.tsx:1-24: geometry comes from the GLB, else the `geometry` prop, else 'the shared unit sphere scaled by size3d at origin3d (v1 primitive)'; anatomyAssets.ts:177-193 explains the content-only set exists precisely because 32 of 38 telencephalon records once fell through to 'a stack of 1 au balls at the origin, visually wrong AND a picking hazard'.
findings.expected: A record with no loadable mesh still has an addressable, correctly placed body (or is deliberately content-only), and a missing/zero anchor cannot produce NaN transforms.
findings.basis: Measured census over the shipped tables and predicates (all layers on): of the 240 records the body pass admits, 133 resolve no committed GLB for any of their own slugs and therefore draw the v1 ellipsoid; ALL 133 carry origin3d and size3d (0 exceptions). Records with no origin3d at all: 30 of 264 — of which 11 also have no manifest slug and no ANATOMY_RECORD_LINKS entry (the cortex/insula surfaces and the three internal-capsule subdivisions), and every one of those 11 is excluded from the body pass by isGhostOrContentOnly (TEL_CONTENT_ONLY_IDS ∪ render:'ghost'), so the '1 au ball at the world origin' class is empty. `explodeDirection([0,0,0])` returns [0,0] (len < 1e-4 guard, curves.ts:35-37), so a zero anchor yields the unshifted position instead of NaN; a record with no size3d takes scale [1,1,1] on the shared sphere (NucleusMesh.tsx:184). Failed-load records stay fully interactive: the pointer handlers live on the mesh element and the fallback body is a real mesh, so click/hover/label work and the info panel opens.
findings.suggestedFix: None. Worth keeping the census as a gate assertion (every body-pass record has either a manifest slug, an ANATOMY_RECORD_LINKS body, or origin3d+size3d) — verify:audit-facts and verify:vessel-render already check the related 'one record, one body' invariant from the other side.
findings.notes: Checked as a brief item ('selecting a structure whose mesh failed to load', 'a record whose origin3d is missing').

findings.subject: All-on scene composition: 442 body meshes + 149 tubes + 10 envelopes + 2 ghost shells + 32 somatotopy patches ≈ 635 drawables, and no gate measures draw calls
findings.field: SceneLayers.tsx:688-843 (bodies, tubes), 356-367 (envelopes), 593-607 (ghost shells), SomatotopyOverlay.tsx (16 segments × 2 hemispheres)
findings.claimed: The v2/v7 performance contract in the plan is expressed as triangles and bytes: README's budget table lists 'Rendered triangles (scene) ≤ 800,000' and 'Committed GLB payload ≤ 14 MiB'; QUALITY_PLAN §3 targets per-frame cost (one frame callback, memoized render order, dpr caps).
findings.expected: If the project budgets scene cost by triangles, either draw calls are also measured (or bounded by construction and stated), or the absence is stated — an unbudgeted draw-call count is how a 'budgeted' scene degrades silently.
findings.basis: Measured composition (shipped predicates, all layers on): 240 records pass isStructureVisible; expanding each record's body list per side (anatomySlugsForRecord, plus the paired/or-`bodyRight` rule at SceneLayers.tsx:784) yields 442 NucleusMesh instances; plus 149 TractTube instances, 10 envelope slots, 2 hemisphere shells and 32 somatotopy patches (16 segments × 2 sides, SomatotopyOverlay). Each body/tube instance owns its own material (NucleusMesh.tsx:164, TractTube.tsx:423), and the envelope/ghost/somatotopy families share module singletons. verify:budget-report measures Σ parts[].triCount and file bytes only; no gate counts meshes, materials or draw calls, and no gate would fail if a change doubled the instance count (e.g. a paired-mirroring rule applied twice). The default framing is much lighter (vessels region off: 70 tubes, and the telencephalon ghost is not a body pass), which is why the all-on state is the one to measure.
findings.suggestedFix: Extend budget-report (or add a sibling) with a structural count derived from the shipped tables: records admitted × bodies per side, tube instances per family, envelope slots, patches — with a stated cap. That is a pure-data computation (no GL context), which is exactly the shape this repo's gates already use.
findings.notes: The triangle half of the same question is rob-002 (a real cap breach); this finding is the 'nothing measures it' half. Chromium's real draw-call count remains orchestrator-only.

findings.subject: The 2D draw loop's per-frame work is memoized and byte-bounded, but Viewer3D's panel hint runs an unconditional 60 Hz rAF poll of a value published at ≤1 Hz
findings.field: SectionCanvas.tsx:1069-1248 (render-order cache + Path2D budget) vs Viewer3D.tsx:582-646 (SectionPipHint tick)
findings.claimed: SectionCanvas header (106-126): 'ONE cache object (RenderOrderCache) is computed only when the render key changes … one Path2D per visible part, reused until the contours change or the transform changes, bounded by a BYTE budget (PATH2D_BUDGET_BYTES) so a long drag cannot accumulate paths'. Viewer3D.tsx:576-581: 'Reads the module-level diagnostics singleton the in-canvas renderer writes every frame (no store round-trip, no React render): one textContent compare per animation frame, and the node stays hidden — zero layout work — while real imagery shows.'
findings.expected: Per-frame work that only changes on a store/plane/data event is event-driven, or the poll is bounded like the sibling tick that stops itself once the data settles (SectionPiP.tsx:608-630 documents and implements that shape for the same diagnostics).
findings.basis: Code path. SectionCanvas' per-frame cost is bounded as documented: the render order is keyed by (axis, plane, layers, selection, syndrome, contour serial, viewport) and rebuilt only on a key change, Path2D reuse is charged against PATH2D_BUDGET_BYTES with eviction, hover uses a fast path over the cached list, and drawing is skipped while the document is hidden. The panel hint, by contrast, arms `requestAnimationFrame(tick)` in a loop that has no idle exit: every frame it reads sectionPipDiagnostics, rebuilds the hint string, and compares `node.textContent`/`node.hidden`. The producer updates that singleton only on a store change and on a 1 s tick that STOPS once both grids are terminal (SectionPiP.tsx:616-630) — so for the whole steady state the 60 Hz loop compares against a value that can only change on a store edit (which itself already schedules a repaint). The comment's premise ('the in-canvas renderer writes every frame') is stale: the in-canvas PiP renderer was retired in v9 (SectionPiP.tsx:251-257 lists the retired rig fields).
findings.suggestedFix: Poll only when something can change: publish through a tiny subscribe/notify pair (the module already has the singleton pattern) and drop the rAF loop, or keep the rAF but stop it when the hint is null and the grids are settled (re-armed by the store subscription). The same shape as SectionPiP's bounded tick would remove the steady-state cost entirely.
findings.notes: Cost is small (one string build + two property compares per frame) but continuous, and it is the only unbounded per-frame loop left in the surfaces this brief covers. The stale premise ('written every frame') is the kind of documentation drift that makes a bounded design look justified.

findings.subject: The tube geometry cache and the section registry are rebuilt from the authored tables only — no Math.random, no time-dependent keys, no per-frame allocation in the plane path
findings.field: TractTube.tsx:87-100 (FNV-1a hash + hashRange), 107-270 (cache + striation clones), sectionAssets.ts:87-131 (TEL_SLUG_OVERRIDES built once from ANATOMY_RECORD_LINKS)
findings.claimed: TractTube.tsx:83 'Deterministic per-tract variation (no Math.random — seeded style)' and 246-256 'One texture clone per distinct repeat (shared across tracts; ~5 total)'; sectionAssets.ts:87-94 explains the slug overrides are DERIVED from the shared record→body table so the two consumers cannot disagree.
findings.expected: Two runs, two mounts and two StrictMode passes produce byte-identical geometry keys and registry contents — i.e. the reproducibility the gates' hash comparisons rely on.
findings.basis: Measured. Every per-course parameter is a pure function of the record id (FNV-1a → END_RATIO/FLATTEN) or of authored fields (tubeRadius → quantized striation repeat, clamped to 2–6 → at most 5 texture clones); `tubeGeometryFor` returns the identical object for a repeated key (measured: second call returns the same BufferGeometry instance; authored vs `#mirror` keys return DIFFERENT objects with x-reflected bounds [−0.494, 24.314] → [−24.314, 0.494]). The registry is rebuilt per call from the same tables: 103 slugs / 103 unique across both families, no duplicate ids in VESSEL_COURSES (0), every vessel course resolves a taxonomy entry (0 unregistered). The derived override table (TEL_SLUG_OVERRIDES) is computed once at module load from ANATOMY_RECORD_LINKS, so it cannot drift from the 3D pass — verify:view-filter-consistency sweeps the 2D/3D agreement case by case.
findings.suggestedFix: None.
findings.notes: Included because determinism is what makes the other findings measurable (counts, keys, reflections) and because the brief asked whether the mirror keying is correct: it is (distinct objects, reflected bounds, stable across calls).
